obstruction.a_trivial_channel: the free spectrum cos E2 = cos^2(theta) prod cos 2p_i - sin^2(theta) is invariant under all 48 signed permutations, so on any set of copies related by a third-turn (cones, or momenta q, Rq, R^2 q) and at every rest point the free tick contributes E(q) times 1. A multiple of the identity changes a and leaves b, |b| and delta unchanged. The coefficient 2/9 lives in E(q) only.
obstruction.b_order: delta belongs to the copy matrix at q = 0; 2/9 is the q^3 coefficient of E. The first-order copy matrix of any source is built from the rest states at the cone points (exact: entries theta/N times Gaussian integers), which carry no dispersion coefficient.
obstruction.c_arithmetic: Lemma 2: a copy matrix with algebraic entries has algebraic cos 3delta; cos(2/3) is transcendental. All first-order copy matrices of the cones are theta/N times Gaussian-integer matrices, so their delta is never 2/9; the carrier matrices are in Q(sqrt5, sqrt-3).
obstruction.d_units: the 2/9 of the period is per cell^2; in the units where the one-tick coefficient is 2/9 it is 2/27. A unit-free phase can equal it only after a choice of momentum unit.
obstruction.e_symmetry: the third-turn is not a symmetry of the alternating tick (section 3; at the cones the turned program differs by Z = diag(1, 1, -1, -1)): a third-turn-covariant copy matrix exists only for a declared source with that symmetry, and (a) to (c) apply to it.
obstruction.beyond_first_order: ARGUED: at higher orders the dispersion enters through real energy denominators of intermediate states, i.e. as weights of lattice sums; no step isolates the q^3 coefficient
obstruction.label: EXACT (a, c, d, e), ARGUED (beyond first order)

two_ninths_shift.test:
Such an operation acts on the period symbol as p -> R p + K. Test, exactly at four rational momenta: is there a constant
4 x 4 matrix V with V U2(p) = U2(Rp + K) V (unitary form) or V conj(U2(p)) = U2(-Rp + K) V (antiunitary form), for the
eight shifts K in {0, pi/2}^3 (U2 is pi-periodic in every component) and for the turn R and its inverse?
Output: koide.json key 'two_ninths_shift'.
two_ninths_shift.label: EXACT

summary.Q_two_thirds: yes, exactly, only at rank two (lightest copy massless, delta = pi/12 by Lemma 3): G-b one even + one odd point source of equal angle on the axis cones (16 pairs; E0+O2 under W and E2+O0 under ZW are covariant circulants a = 2, |b| = sqrt2, arg b = 3pi/4); G-e particle along a body diagonal with loads on a face or belt triple plus one port (144 cases, not covariant). sqrt reading only (mass reading 0.5505). Rank three needs >= 10 equal sources (G-b; 4 covariant patterns up to 12, delta 0.0855) or tuned angles. G-a never.
summary.delta_two_ninths: never: Lemma 2 (algebraic copy matrices have algebraic cos 3delta; cos(2/3) transcendental); rest-phase readings give 0.27 to 0.90. Nearest natural: pi/15 (T5 face sum), 0.2117 (G-b covariant rank two, Q = 19/27), 0.2709 (M3 kernel). Lemma 3prime: rank two with delta = 2/9 has Q = 0.695325.
summary.body_diagonal_2_9: cannot enter a third-turn-covariant phase: (a) the free spectrum is a function on the cubic group and identical at all 32 rest points, so it adds E(q) times 1 to every copy matrix (a only); (b) delta is a q^0 quantity, 2/9 a q^3 coefficient; (c) Lemma 2; (d) the coefficient depends on the momentum unit (period: -2/9 per cell^2 = -2/27 in DP units; one-tick DP automaton: -+2/9 in DP units = 2 sqrt3/9 in cells); (e) no on-site unitary or antiunitary, plain or staggered, realises the turn on the period (exact nullspaces 0; half-turn control 2).

lemmas.3: rank two and Q = 2/3 <=> ratio 2 - sqrt3 <=> delta = pi/12
